clue.text: Oddly suppressed goodbyes and affirmative word about to finish a long story

indicators.note: to finish says the reversed word comes at the end, after the kept letters
with the odd-numbered letters of goodbyes suppressed, only the even ones are kept
about says the affirmative word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: yes is the affirmative word

explanation.surface: Someone stifles their farewells and a final yes to wrap up a lengthy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly suppressed' drops G, O, B, E from GOODBYES, leaving ODYS; 'about' turns YES into SEY, which 'to finish' puts at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Odyssey is the long epic of Odysseus's voyage home, and the word now means any lengthy saga or journey.

clue.text: Figure with underworld connections has police force breaking up stag?

indicators.note: breaking up says the police force splits the stag word apart by sitting inside it

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure with criminal connections has the police disrupting a stag party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld connections' suggests gangland, but the figure is a goddess linked to Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeter is the Greek goddess whose daughter Persephone was taken to the underworld by Hades, tying her to that realm.

clue.text: Some deadly things that could captivate crew, essentially

definitions.text: Some deadly things that could captivate crew, essentially

indicators.note: captivate means hold captive, so the sins hold the middle letters inside them

parts.note: the seven deadly sins, so some deadly things are sins

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the middle letters of crew

explanation.surface: A warning about lethal lures that might enthral a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: SINS holding RE, the core of 'crew'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Sirens sang so beautifully that passing sailors were lured to their deaths on the rocks.

clue.text: Swordsman removes sheath to seize throne for the Vatican?

indicators.note: to seize means the trimmed swordsman grips the throne word inside it
the sheath is the outer covering, so the swordsman loses his first and last letters

parts.note: a fencer is a swordsman in the sport of fencing
throne is slang for a toilet, and lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: A swordsman unsheathes his weapon to seize a throne on the Pope's behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throne' looks papal but is the toilet, LAV; 'removes sheath' strips FENCER to ENCE, which then holds LAV.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican City is a tiny state wholly surrounded by Rome, a classic example of territory enclosed within another country.

clue.text: 17D 9D in the language of Dubliners?

parts.note: 17 down is FLOWER, and an iris is a flower
9 down is HENRY, and H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle asking how a pairing of entries would be put by Dublin locals.
explanation.walkthrough: Dubliners is also Joyce's story collection, fitting the Ulysses theme; Bloom's pen name in Ulysses is Henry Flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is the Gaelic tongue of Ireland, whose capital is Dublin, so it is the native language of the city's people.

clue.text: Musical sort from Gibraltar with heavenly body

parts.note: Gibraltar is nicknamed the Rock
a star is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: A musician hailing from Gibraltar who has a glamorous physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' hints at a gorgeous figure, but it is simply a star in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock star is a famous performer of rock music, so a musical type of person.

clue.text: Endure a term of French to climb up through school

indicators.note: through says the climbing piece passes through the school abbreviation, sitting inside it
in a down clue, climbing up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: mot is the French word for word, a term

explanation.surface: Putting up with a term of French lessons in order to rise through the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To climb up' reverses A MOT to TOMA, which goes 'through' SCH as S-TOMA-CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or put up with it, an idiom drawn from being able to digest food.

clue.text: Like more than a few games, they may be fixed

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
in tennis a set is made up of several games

explanation.surface: A suspicious remark that many matches might be rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' suggests match-fixing in the surface, but it points to fixed assets in accounting.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed assets are a firm's long-term property such as buildings and machinery, so assets are things that may be fixed.

clue.text: In final parts of tour, castrati lip-sync to such old lines

parts.note: in can mean at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: final parts are the last letters of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: On the last legs of a tour, the castrati mime along to their songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but gives HOME, as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeric describes the epic verse of Homer, the ancient Greek poet of the Iliad and Odyssey, so such old lines of poetry.

clue.text: Jean Rhys novel inspires your setter to become an author

indicators.note: inspires is read as breathes in, so the rearranged name takes the setter inside it
novel means new, so the letters of the name are arranged anew

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A Jean Rhys novel motivates the compiler to try writing professionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book by Jean Rhys but signals the anagram: JEAN RHYS gives HENRYJAS, and 'inspires' takes ME inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was the American-born novelist of The Portrait of a Lady and The Turn of the Screw.

clue.text: A side of arsenic fed to awfully sly cop who detained hero

indicators.note: fed to says one letter is put into the rearranged words
awfully means badly, so the letters of sly cop are jumbled
a side of the word arsenic here is its final edge, the last letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful, shifty policeman is poisoned with arsenic after locking someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: The same wording, with 'one' added, clues 28 across using the other side of 'arsenic'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey the one-eyed giant Polyphemus, a Cyclops, trapped Odysseus and his men in his cave.

clue.text: Charming lady left out of social group

indicators.note: out of says the letter for left is removed from the group word

parts.note: a circle is a social group, as in a circle of friends

explanation.surface: A delightful woman has been excluded from her set of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' sounds like plain pleasantness; here it means casting charms, as an enchantress does.
explanation.definitionFit: Circe is the sorceress of the Odyssey who turned Odysseus's crew into swine, so a woman who works charms or spells.

clue.text: Lady Godiva's habit was so unacceptable

definitions.meaning: Lady Godiva rode naked, so her clothing, her riding habit
a British idiom meaning not acceptable

explanation.surface: A disapproving comment on Lady Godiva's notorious naked ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' means riding clothes, not custom. Lady Godiva is the legendary noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not on means it is out of order or unacceptable; literally, clothes not on describes nakedness.

clue.text: Group invested in ice cap so ready to flip over business with astronauts

indicators.note: flipping over means the run of letters reads backwards
a group of letters is invested in, held inside, the words that follow

explanation.surface: A consortium has put money into an ice cap and is ready to turn it upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group invested in' sounds financial but marks a run inside 'ice cap so ready'; 'to flip over' reads that run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The aerospace industry builds aircraft and spacecraft, the commercial field that sends astronauts into orbit.

clue.text: At first, young author regretted novelising rambling tale

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A writer in their youth later regretted turning a long-winded story into a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long, often meandering story, from sailors spinning tales as they spun rope.

clue.text: Youngster seeking old man Methuselah sadly getting cold, not hot

indicators.note: sadly means badly or regrettably, so the letters are rearranged
getting introduces the letter that comes into the name
not marks the letter that is taken out to make room

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A young person searches for an elderly man while the setter, Methuselah, sadly catches a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is the setter's own pseudonym. 'Getting cold, not hot' swaps one H for C, and 'sadly' scrambles the result.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey, Telemachus is the son of Odysseus who sets out in search of news of his long-absent father.

clue.text: Stars lie low every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then means taking only some letters, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Celebrities keep out of sight from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is a constellation and zodiac sign, a group of stars said to depict a lion.

clue.text: Mother of 14 to run away with writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, a writer
to elope is to run away to marry

explanation.surface: A mother runs off with an author, abandoning her many children.
explanation.walkthrough: '14' is the answer to 14 across, TELEMACHUS, not a number of children.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope, faithful wife of Odysseus, is the mother of Telemachus in Homer's Odyssey.

clue.text: Roadside staff giving directions using index cards, maybe?

parts.note: the index is the pointing finger
cards, such as postcards, are an example of post, mail

explanation.surface: Someone finds their way by consulting a set of index cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but means a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingerpost is a signpost at a road junction, with arms shaped like pointing fingers showing the way.

clue.text: Bloom's upset about modernist writer losing heart

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, reading the letters backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the writer's name drops out

parts.note: Virginia Woolf was a leading modernist novelist

explanation.surface: A man named Bloom is distressed about a modernist author's lack of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart' trims WOOLF to WOLF; 'upset' turns RE plus WOLF upside down. Leopold Bloom of Ulysses writes as Henry Flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloom is a blossom on a plant, a direct synonym for this word.

clue.text: Dangerous liquid offered by new Australian pub that doesn't close

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house, a pub

indicators.note: doesn't close means the word that loses its final letter, its closing letter

explanation.surface: A risky drink served by a new Aussie bar that never shuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't close' sounds like round-the-clock opening hours, but cuts the last letter from 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a highly flammable hydrocarbon mixture used as a solvent and fuel, hence hazardous.

clue.text: Suggest what Teletubbies might say when charging round the playground

definitions.meaning: to put forward an idea, to suggest

definitions.text: what Teletubbies might say when charging round the playground
definitions.meaning: Po is a Teletubby; in a game of tag the chaser is it

explanation.surface: A playful thought about children's TV characters playing tag at break time.
explanation.walkthrough: Teletubbies is a British pre-school TV series whose characters include Po; in tag, whoever chases is 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit means to propose or put forward as a premise, which is to suggest.

clue.text: Two companies with conflicting directions get superior fellow on blower

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the fellow comes first

parts.note: sir is a title or form of address for a superior man
CO is company; one reads backwards and one forwards, giving OC and CO

explanation.surface: Two firms pulling opposite ways have a senior man on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blower' looks like British slang for a telephone, but it means a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot, dusty wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean, so a blower in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Air kiss when knight travels east

indicators.note: in an across answer east is rightwards, so the knight's letter shifts along to the right

parts.note: snog is British slang for a passionate kiss
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A blown kiss as a chess knight makes its move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air kiss' reads as one phrase, but 'Air' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, as in a simple song.

clue.text: Democrat quits at end of four years somewhere in Washington

indicators.note: quits at end of means the party letter leaves from the final position of the period word

parts.note: an Olympiad is the four-year period between Olympic Games

explanation.surface: A Democrat steps down when a four-year term ends in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' suggests DC politics, but it is the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia is the state capital of Washington State in the US Pacific Northwest, so a place there.

clue.text: Delight in a bit of wind with love

parts.note: a gust is a brief burst of wind
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Taking pleasure in a breeze and in romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment or relish, so taking delight in something.

clue.text: Another word for 5 sounds like French in some accents

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is heard the same as the word for French
in some accents limits the match to certain ways of speaking, such as Scottish

parts.note: Gallic means French, from Gaul

explanation.surface: A word for Irish that can sound like a French word, depending on the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 across is IRISH. Gaelic is usually said GAY-lik, but in Scotland it is said GAL-ik, like Gallic.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaelic is the Celtic language of Ireland, so another name for Irish as a language.

clue.text: He has people under him work with iron and gold

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to press clothes is to iron them
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A boss with staff below him at a metalworking business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He has people under him' sounds like a manager, but here it means keeping people down.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor is a tyrant who keeps others subjugated, holding them under his control.

clue.text: Profound gap year stops sailor getting to ship

indicators.note: stops means the year letter closes off the sailor, coming right after him

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A gap year comes to an end when a sailor reaches his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profound' looks like deep thought but means physically deep; 'gap year' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm, a very deep opening in the earth.

clue.text: Some deadbeat southerner patronises restaurateur

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A layabout from the south is a regular customer of a restaurant owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patronises' suggests condescension, but here it means being a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat out is to dine at a restaurant, giving custom to the person who runs it.

clue.text: A side of arsenic fed to awfully sly cop — one who detained hero

indicators.note: fed to says one letter is put into the rearranged words
awfully means badly, so the letters of sly cop are jumbled
a side of the word arsenic here is its starting edge, the first letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful, shifty policeman is poisoned with arsenic after locking someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: This repeats 10 across's wording; here the other side of 'arsenic' goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey the nymph Calypso kept Odysseus captive on her island of Ogygia for seven years.

clue.text: See 9
Church article on rapture is reminiscent of Famous 5 writer

indicators.note: in an across answer on means coming after, so the church and article follow the rapture

parts.note: joy is rapture, great delight
CE is the Church of England
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A church text on ecstasy that recalls Enid Blyton's children's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous 5' looks like Enid Blyton's Famous Five, but 5 is IRISH: a famous Irish writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Joycean describes the style of James Joyce, the celebrated Irish author of Ulysses.
